properties.name: An HTTP server told to stop drains its work in progress, writes a waiting export, closes every store, then exits
properties.rationale:
req:a-server-drains-before-it-stops, the third engine "now" item, on @ajs's word ("Yes, let's build the now items in reflow2"; then "finish the clean-shutdown item, then start step 3"). Combined plan position 1 of 10.

OBSERVED BEFORE THE CHANGE, on the released 0.72.0 binary: a --http server with --export-to, written to and then sent SIGTERM inside the two-second quiet period, died with status 143 and the export did not contain the write. There was no signal handler at all on the non-shared HTTP paths.

MEASURED ON flo2.io THE SAME NIGHT (read-only): the reflow2 container's process 1 is /usr/local/bin/reflow2-mcp itself (the image's sh entrypoint execs it), with no --init and Docker's default stop timeout. A process 1 with no handler ignores SIGTERM, and the nightly flo2-backup logged "stopping reflow2" and "reflow2 restarted" 10 s, 10 s and 11 s apart on 2026-09-25, -26 and -27 — Docker's full stop timeout, then SIGKILL. That wait is the "about 10 s" pause the backup has been recorded as costing; with a handler that drains, the stop takes as long as the work in progress.

WHY A GET IS NOT WORK: in MCP's streamable HTTP transport a GET is the standalone server-to-client stream and lives as long as its session; counting it would make every stop wait out the grace. A tool call is a POST whose answer stream ends once the answer is sent.

WHY 5 s: Docker's default stop timeout is 10 s; grace 5 s plus the 2 s close bound fits inside it. Kubernetes (30 s) and systemd (90 s) operators can raise it.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: New module drain.rs; every --http server (one design, --registry-root, the shared server) now serves through it. On SIGTERM or SIGINT: stop accepting; each connection finishes its exchange and closes; every request that is not a GET is work, and gets up to --shutdown-grace (new flag, default 5s) to finish; rmcp's cancellation token ends sessions and streams; a write-through export still waiting is flushed (AutoExport::flush); every design closes and its store is released within 2 s (GraphRouter::close_all for a registry, which also answers 503 to anything arriving after); the server exits 0 and says on stderr what it did, including requests cut off by the grace. A second signal exits at once. A shared server's rendezvous comes down when the stop begins, and its idle expiry drains the same way instead of exit(0). The write-through task now holds the design weakly, so it never keeps a closed store open.
